clue.text: Power to limit urban growth?

parts.note: to cap something is to put a ceiling on it
a city is what urban growth produces; the question mark flags the loose sense

explanation.surface: A planning question: does a council have the power to restrict a town's expansion?
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'to limit urban growth' as an instruction: cap a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity means ability or power to do something, as in 'in my capacity as chair'.

clue.text: Ursa Minor appearing over a Caribbean island

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece appearing over another is written above it, so first

parts.note: Ursa Minor is Latin for the Little Bear, and a little bear is a cub
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes the Little Bear constellation rising above a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Wine left for someone in schooner, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fortified wine from Portugal

definitions.text: left for someone in schooner, say
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word sailors use for the left-hand side of a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: A schooner is also a large glass for sherry or beer, so the surface pictures a drink being poured; here it is the sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is both a sweet fortified wine and the nautical term for a ship's left side.

clue.text: Demolished canards as prognosticator, unbelievably accurate

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its parts can be rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone's false rumours are torn apart by a forecaster who turned out to be right.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassandra, the Trojan prophetess, was cursed always to foretell the truth and never be believed: hence 'unbelievably accurate'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Cassandra's prophecies were true but nobody believed them, so she is the archetypal disbelieved forecaster.

clue.text: As something required in court state, in brief, one's crime

parts.note: TENN is the short form of Tennessee
one is I, and 's stands for is
a racket is a criminal scheme

explanation.surface: A courtroom defendant summarises their offence in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis racket is the equipment a player needs on a tennis court.

clue.text: Its content suffers shell damage before soldiers go in

definitions.text: Its content suffers shell damage before soldiers go in

parts.words: Its content suffers shell damage before soldiers go in
parts.note: surface reading: a fortified position is bombarded before an infantry assault

parts.words: Its content suffers shell damage before soldiers go in
parts.note: setter's reading: a boiled egg has its top cracked off, then strips of toast are dipped in

explanation.surface: Artillery pounds a position before the troops advance into it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin fingers of buttered toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: An eggcup holds a boiled egg upright while its shell is broken and toast is dunked into the yolk.

clue.text: Cross, perhaps, about one condition of course

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: gong is slang for a medal, such as the Victoria Cross
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about the state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is a medal, slangily a gong.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing the going is the state of the ground on the racecourse, from firm to heavy.

clue.text: Unreliable in island about evidence of debt

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
C is short for circa, meaning about
IOUs are written promises to pay, so evidence that money is owed

explanation.surface: A shaky report about debts on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricious means changeable and impulsive, so not to be relied upon.

clue.text: Publicity expert's gift in decline? Just the opposite

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, read literally as the gift inside the decline
this phrase swaps the roles, so whichever piece was to go inside now goes outside instead

parts.note: a gift is a present
to sag is to droop or decline

explanation.surface: Is a publicist's talent fading? No, it is the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the gift goes inside the decline; 'Just the opposite' reverses that, so the decline goes inside the gift. The definition's 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A press agent is employed to get publicity for a client in newspapers and broadcasts.

clue.text: Way boy interrupts important series of tweets

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

parts.note: big means important, as in a big decision
RD is the abbreviation for road
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad breaks into a significant run of social-media posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweets' suggests posts online, but here they are literal bird calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdsong is the run of musical calls a bird makes, and a bird's call is a tweet.

clue.text: Flower person found in fruit tart

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: A florist spots something inside a fruit pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' suggests hiding, but it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Flower people, or flower children, was the 1960s name for hippies, who wore flowers as a peace emblem.

clue.text: Collective panic as dodgy operator enters train going north

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it
in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to train a weapon on a target is to aim it
taken as written
a shyster is an unscrupulous dealer, especially a crooked lawyer

explanation.surface: Crowds panic when a crooked figure boards a northbound train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' reads as a railway train, but it is the verb meaning to point a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass hysteria is irrational fear or excitement spreading through a whole group at once.

clue.text: Some taxable income from Honolulu and Juneau in 1959, for the States

parts.note: straight reading: profits on investments that are subject to tax

parts.words: from Honolulu and Juneau in 1959, for the States
parts.note: setter's reading: Hawaii and Alaska became states in 1959, so the USA acquired these two state capital cities

explanation.surface: A tax question about earnings from Hawaii and Alaska in a particular year.
explanation.walkthrough: Honolulu is Hawaii's capital and Juneau is Alaska's; both territories joined the Union in 1959.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital gains are profits made on selling assets, taxed in both Britain and the USA.

clue.text: Unusually, opera introducing learner is well covered

indicators.note: to be covered is to have something wrapped round you

parts.note: ably means well, competently

indicators.note: the opera introduces the learner, so it comes first with the learner straight after

parts.note: Norma is Bellini's opera
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: An opera production that adds a novice singer is unusually well funded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introducing' just puts the learner after the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormally means in a way that departs from the norm, which is what happens unusually.

clue.text: Change in menu, alas, like certain changes of time forward or back

definitions.text: like certain changes of time forward or back

indicators.note: a change alters the arrangement, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A diner laments that the menu has been altered again.
explanation.walkthrough: Clocks go forward in spring and back in autumn, so the change happens twice a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Semi-annual means occurring every half year, like the spring and autumn clock changes.

clue.text: Part of double-edged sword could make you do this

definitions.text: sword could make you do this

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two halves

explanation.surface: A warning that a two-sided blade can draw blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the hyphen: dou-BLE ED-ged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut from a sword makes you lose blood, so the clue's sword is what makes you bleed.

clue.text: Putting in other words a little time into relaxation

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: resting is relaxing
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time, a little of the word

explanation.surface: Rephrasing something while fitting a short break into one's downtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Restating means saying again in a different way, that is rephrasing.

clue.text: Improperly notarises claim

indicators.note: improperly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A notary wrongly certifies a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident statement that something is so, the same as a claim.

clue.text: As a rule, its leaders are unlikely to get to number ten

definitions.text: As a rule, its leaders are unlikely to get to number ten

parts.words: As a rule, its leaders are unlikely to get to number ten
parts.note: surface reading: some group's leaders generally will not reach Downing Street

parts.words: As a rule, its leaders are unlikely to get to number ten
parts.note: setter's reading: a form of rule whose leaders are few, numbering fewer than ten

explanation.surface: A political party's leaders seldom make it to 10 Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' looks like 'usually' but means 'as a form of government'; 'number ten' is a count, not the PM's address.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is government by a small group of people, from Greek for rule of the few.

clue.text: Slight encouragement needed by leading character in novel

parts.note: a spur is an incentive

indicators.note: the leading character is the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of novel

explanation.surface: A writer needs only a little encouragement to bring a protagonist into their book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective meaning small, but it is the verb meaning to snub.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub them, and to spurn is to reject with contempt.

clue.text: RLS and TSE, for example

parts.note: surface reading: two strings of capital letters, like abbreviations
setter's reading: Robert Louis Stevenson and T S Eliot, writers known by their initials

explanation.walkthrough: Both are famous authors commonly referred to by their initials, so they are writers and also men made of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Men of letters are literary scholars and authors, and these two writers are identified by letters alone.

clue.text: In place of advance, surrender

parts.note: for can mean instead of, as in swapping one for another
to go forward is to advance

explanation.surface: Instead of pushing forward, an army gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to give something up, to renounce or surrender it.

clue.text: Producer of notes originating on back of envelope

indicators.note: originating means beginning, so only where each word starts is used

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Somebody jots notes on the back of an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests jottings, but they are musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, and an instrument produces musical notes.

clue.text: Get out vote in no-win situation going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a tie is a result where nobody wins
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Getting voters out in a deadlocked contest that is going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: a way out, as on a door sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out of a building, so a sign that says how to get out.

clue.text: Museum showing the collected work of artist there, apart from one piece

indicators.note: apart from one piece means everything except one letter is kept

parts.words: the collected work of artist there
parts.note: in French, l'oeuvre is an artist's whole body of work; 'there' points to France

explanation.surface: A gallery displays an artist's complete works, all but one item.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the E from L'OEUVRE, the French term for collected works.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most visited art museum.

clue.text: Clever clogs and article of clothing packed

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
something packed is in a box

explanation.surface: A know-all and a garment stuffed into luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: Clever clogs is British slang for a smart person, often a show-off; 'clogs' tempts a reading as footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainbox is British informal for a very intelligent person, the same as a clever clogs.

clue.text: Audibly react to blow, maybe, being cowardly

parts.note: to yell is to react by shouting
ow is the cry of pain at being hit

explanation.surface: Crying out when struck shows a lack of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for cowardly, as in having a yellow streak.

clue.text: For instance, an anagram that's shrewd in the extreme

indicators.note: the clue openly says to rearrange the preceding word's letters

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A setter offers an example of a particularly clever rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd, so the superlative canniest means most shrewd.
